original_question: For binary words of length n, let XNL(n) denote the maximum possible number of pairwise non-equivalent abelian square factors, where an abelian square is a factor uv with matching Parikh vectors and two abelian squares are non-equivalent when their Parikh vectors differ. Is XNL(n) always bounded above by a constant multiple of n^1.5?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 0.2 in the section "The maximum number of abelian squares in a linear word"; in the survey’s notation this is the upper-bound conjecture for XNL(n), i.e. the binary linear-word version of the conjecture attributed to [13].
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the binary setting, the extremal function XNL(n), the fact that one is counting nonequivalent abelian-square factors rather than occurrences, the use of Parikh vectors to define equivalence, and the intended asymptotic upper bound O(n^(3/2)).
missing_details: The paper is about linear words here, not circular words; that distinction matters because the paper treats circular variants separately.
A factor should be stated to mean a contiguous subword.
XNL(n) is the maximum over all binary words of length n of the number of equivalence classes of abelian-square factors occurring in the word; this excludes multiplicity.
The big-O quantifier should be made explicit: there exists an absolute constant C such that XNL(n) <= C n^(3/2) for all positive integers n (or equivalently for all sufficiently large n).
The paper’s conjecture is presented in the context of the known lower bound immediately preceding it, so the question should be anchored to that same extremal function and notation.
The exact target is Conjecture 0.2 as attributed to reference [13]; the draft omits that paper-faithful provenance.
refined_question: For each positive integer n, let XNL(n) be the maximum, over all binary linear words w of length n, of the number of equivalence classes of abelian-square factors occurring in w, where a factor means a contiguous subword, an abelian square is a factor uv with equal Parikh vectors, and two abelian-square factors are equivalent iff they have the same Parikh vector. Is there an absolute constant C such that XNL(n) <= C n^(3/2) for all n >= 1?
justification: This draft is aiming at the survey’s Conjecture 0.2 in the subsection on the maximum number of abelian squares in a linear word. The surrounding context first defines abelian squares, equivalence via Parikh vectors, and the notation XNL(n) for the binary linear-word extremal problem, then records a lower bound for XNL(n), and then states Conjecture 0.2. In the HTML extraction of the survey, the displayed formula of Conjecture 0.2 is dropped, but the survey explicitly identifies [13] as Kociumaka–Radoszewski–Rytter–Walén (DLT 2014), and that cited paper’s Conjecture 1 is precisely the upper-bound statement SQ'_Abel(n,2)=O(n^1.5), which translates into the survey’s notation as XNL(n)=O(n^(3/2)). So your draft is very close to the paper-faithful target; it mainly needs the linear/contiguous-factor scope and the quantifiers made explicit.
